metaTitle: Toni's Sushi Bar Instagram Case Study | Button Up Media
metaDescription: How Button Up Media grew Toni's Sushi Bar on South Beach from about 4K to 80K Instagram followers in five months, with Reels of its chef that drew 64M+ views.
ldHeadline: Toni's Sushi Bar: from about 4K to 80K Instagram followers in five months
h1Sub: 4K to 80K Instagram followers in five months
answer: In our Reels, the chef at Toni's Sushi Bar teaches how to eat sushi. Followers grew from about 4K to 80K in five months, and 22 Reels drew 64M+ views.

hero.alt: Chef Toshiya at Toni's Sushi Bar showing the right way to dip nigiri in soy sauce, from the Reel with 52.5M views

metrics.label: Instagram followers, up from about 4K
metrics.meaning: About 4,000 people followed @tonissushi when our first Reel went up on June 18, 2026. Five months later, on Nov 16, 2026, the account had 80,100 followers, about 20 times as many.

metrics.label: Reel views in five months
metrics.meaning: We added up the views Instagram shows on all 22 Reels we posted from June 18 to Nov 16, 2026. They also collected 1.9M+ likes.

metrics.label: Views on one Reel
metrics.meaning: This is the chef's sushi etiquette lesson, posted Aug 19, 2026. It has 1.6M likes and is pinned at the top of the profile.

reels.h2: The 4 Reels that passed 1 million views
reels.intro: Tap any Reel to watch it with sound. View counts are what Instagram showed on Nov 16, 2026.

paragraphs: Toni's has been family-run on South Beach since 1987, when Hiromi “Toni” Takarada opened it, according to Miami New Times. Its Instagram calls it South Beach's original sushi bar.
Its Instagram didn't show much of that history. The account had about 4,000 followers, and its last posts before we started, in February 2026, got 12 to 156 likes each.

items.title: Put the chef in front of the camera
items.bodyHtml: Chef Toshiya, a sushi chef from Japan, explains on camera how sushi is eaten in Japan. For example, soy sauce goes on the fish instead of the rice, ginger is eaten between pieces, and there's no need to rub your chopsticks together.

items.title: Teach one thing per Reel
items.bodyHtml: Each video covers one topic, like real wasabi versus the green paste, the difference between sashimi, temaki and nigiri, or the three cuts of bluefin tuna. Short lessons are easy to save and send to a friend, which is how they reach people who don't follow the account yet.

items.title: Leave the sales pitch out
items.bodyHtml: None of the Reels ask people to come eat at Toni's. The idea is that watching a chef from Japan teach the proper way to eat sushi gives people their own reason to visit.

items.title: Point viewers to the restaurant
items.bodyHtml: We put the address, 1208 Washington Ave, in the comments of every Reel. On the etiquette Reel, that comment has 2,624 likes. Our Instagram Stories also point people who just watched a Reel to the restaurant and show them how to get there.

items.title: of all Reel views came from the etiquette lesson
items.body: The sushi etiquette Reel has 52.5M of the 64.7M views across all 22 Reels. It's pinned at the top of the profile, so it's the first post people see when they open the account.

items.title: Reels past 1M views show the chef teaching
items.body: Those three are the soy sauce etiquette Reel, the real wasabi Reel and the chopstick Reel. Lessons like these are easy to share, and shares are how a Reel reaches people who don't follow the account yet.

items.title: is about how often we posted a new Reel
items.body: We posted 22 Reels in 21 weeks, mostly built around the chef teaching one thing. In that time the account went from about 4K followers to 80.1K.
